You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company) — customer; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI) — vendor/host.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

paragraphs.text: SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT

This SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT (the "Agreement") dated as of August 9, 1999 is made between Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI"), a New Jersey Corporation, located at 1500 Harbor Boulevard, Weehawken, NJ 07087, and The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company"), a Nevada corporation, located at 2500 Arrowhead Drive, Carson City, NV 89706. Each of the parties hereto shall be referred to as a "Party".
In consideration of the mutual promises and covenants set forth below, HDI and the Company agree as follows:
1. HDI's Responsibilities.

1.1 HDI shall design, develop, implement, operate, maintain and manage, and enable the Company to establish a presence on the World Wide Web ("Site") to make available to Internet users on demand, men's and women's apparel and accessories from the Deerskin Catalog ("Deerskin Products"). As used in this Agreement, "Deerskin Products" shall not include (i) closeout merchandise which the Company may identify as "Deerskin" branded items, if such is the case, nor (ii) products from the Company's Joan Cook Catalog.
1.2 HDI shall bear all costs associated with the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance and management of the Site, including, without limitation, technology and labor.
1.3 HDI shall host and maintain the Site on a server provided by HDI.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, minimum volume, or take-or-pay obligation binding the Company:

- **§3.1 (Fees)** — the only payment obligation is 30% of Net Sales *in excess of* $11,000 per calendar month. This is purely transaction-based; the $11,000 threshold operates in our favour as a floor below which nothing is owed, not as a minimum spend.
- **§4.1 (Term)** — one-year term with annual auto-renewal, terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice; **§1.6** gives us an additional unilateral termination right without penalty if the Site is not operational within 70 days. No multi-year lock-in.
- No "shortfall", "minimum", or committed-volume language appears anywhere in the document.

Two adjacent points noted in the rationale but not flagged under this rule (to avoid double-counting commercial terms):
- **§4.2 Termination Payment** — if we terminate, we owe half of trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000. This is an exit cost, not a purchase commitment, and belongs to the termination-fee rule.
- **§6.1 Exclusivity** — restricts the Company from similar Deerskin internet projects; an exclusivity issue rather than a volume cap on usage.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

This is a bounded short-document repair and you have no tools. The user supplies the exact source paragraphs, definitions, current proposal, and deterministic feedback. Return only the requested structured proposal and one-to-one element coverage. Copy every replace.oldText byte-for-byte from a supplied paragraph. Do not invent an anchor or source text.

Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Position — preferred:

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:

Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. input.summary: Insert new Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide transition assistance and return/delete Company data on termination.
input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is silent on exit: HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and customer data, but owes us nothing back on termination. We have added a standard transition-assistance and data-return provision (up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of data within 30 days in a machine-readable format, then certified deletion). We can accept 90 days of assistance if six months is an issue, but return of our data within 30 days is required.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days of the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer data and other Confidential Information of the Company then in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content, user information, customer data and other Confidential Information from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Rule: LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

Preferred position:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.

Fallback position:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
4.2 Termination Payment.
(a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
(b) In the event that the amount of the Termination
Payment is determined pursuant to this Section 4.2 to be less than or equal to zero, then no Termination Payment shall be due to HDI nor shall HDI be required to make any termination payment to the Company if the amount is determined to be less than zero.
(c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.

4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
4.2 Termination Payment.
(a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI no termination payment, penalty or liquidated damages, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be zero and not an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
(b) In the event that the amount of the Termination
Payment is determined pursuant to this Section 4.2 to be less than or equal to zero, then no Termination Payment shall be due to HDI nor shall HDI be required to make any termination payment to the Company if the amount is determined to be less than zero.
(c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.

input.quote: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
input.rationale: Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; there is no exit, transition-assistance, data-return, migration or deletion provision anywhere in the Agreement. This is a site development and hosting agreement in which HDI operates the Site on its own server (Sections 1.3, 1.4) and holds our Content, user information and customer data (Section 8.1), so on termination we would have no contractual right to recover that data or to obtain migration help. The confidentiality provisions (8.1-8.2) restrict use and disclosure but do not require return or deletion, and the survival clause (10.7) does not fill the gap. Playbook expects at minimum 90 days of transition assistance and data export within 30 days; nothing here meets even the fallback, so we insert a new Section 4.3 at the preferred position (up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion).

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide transition assistance and return/delete Company data on termination.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is silent on exit: HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and customer data, but owes us nothing back on termination. We have added a standard transition-assistance and data-return provision (up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of data within 30 days in a machine-readable format, then certified deletion). We can accept 90 days of assistance if six months is an issue, but return of our data within 30 days is required.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days of the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer data and other Confidential Information of the Company then in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content, user information, customer data and other Confidential Information from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company) — customer; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI) — vendor/host.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert new Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide transition assistance and return/delete Company data on termination.
input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is silent on exit: HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and customer data, but owes us nothing back on termination. We have added a standard transition-assistance and data-return provision (up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of data within 30 days in a machine-readable format, then certified deletion). We can accept 90 days of assistance if six months is an issue, but return of our data within 30 days is required.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days of the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer data and other Confidential Information of the Company then in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content, user information, customer data and other Confidential Information from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company.

input.quote: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
input.rationale: Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) addresses only notice periods and the Termination Payment; there is no exit, transition-assistance, data-return, migration or deletion provision anywhere in the Agreement. This is a site development and hosting agreement in which HDI operates the Site on its own server (Sections 1.3, 1.4) and holds our Content, user information and customer data (Section 8.1), so on termination we would have no contractual right to recover that data or to obtain migration help. The confidentiality provisions (8.1-8.2) restrict use and disclosure but do not require return or deletion, and the survival clause (10.7) does not fill the gap. Playbook expects at minimum 90 days of transition assistance and data export within 30 days; nothing here meets even the fallback, so we insert a new Section 4.3 at the preferred position (up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion).

content.text:
**Finding: MISSING** (medium severity, confidence 0.86)

**What I checked:** Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment — p0023–p0029), Section 1 (HDI's hosting responsibilities), Section 8 (Confidentiality), and Section 10.7 (Survival). I also searched for "termination," "Content," and data-return language across the whole document.

**Why it's missing:** Section 4 covers only the renewal/notice mechanics and the Termination Payment formula. There is no exit, transition, migration, data-export or deletion provision anywhere. That gap matters here because HDI hosts the Site on its own server (1.3), controls the system on which the Site is stored (1.4), and is expressly exposed to our "Content, user information, data... and trade secret information" (8.1). The confidentiality obligations restrict use and disclosure but never require return or deletion, and the survival clause (10.7) doesn't reach Section 4. On termination we would have no right to recover our own data or to any migration help — below even the playbook fallback of 90 days' assistance plus 30-day export.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** New Section 4.3 inserted after p0029, at the preferred position — up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates including Site migration cooperation, return of Content/user information/customer data within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification. The accompanying comment flags 90 days of assistance as an acceptable fallback while holding firm on the 30-day data return.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

Rule: TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return

Preferred position:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.


Fallback position:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
4.2 Termination Payment.
(c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.

Rendered redlined clause:
4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
4.2 Termination Payment.
(c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.
4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information and customer data of the Company then in HDI's possession or control, in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content, user information and customer data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-license-fe02a09e","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 1.4 is the only inbound grant to us (the other licence, at p0038, runs from us to HDI and is out of scope). The grant of \"access to, and the right to use\" HDI's hosting system and administration tools is limited to \"the Company\" alone: it names neither our affiliates nor contractors acting on our behalf, and gives no mechanism (e.g. written notice) to add them, so it fails even the fallback position. It is also silent on revocability, leaving HDI room to argue access may be withdrawn at will. Section 10.3 (Assignment) binds successors and assigns, so successor transfer is largely covered, but affiliate/contractor scope is not. We propose a short subsection extending the rights to affiliates and contractors, confirming they are not revocable at HDI's discretion (only for uncured material breach or on termination), and confirming successor transferability; affiliate coverage on prior written notice is offered as a fallback.","proposal":"Extend the Section 1.4 access/use rights to Company affiliates and contractors, make them non-revocable at will and transferable to a successor.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-02b8a10e","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 6.1 does impose a field-of-use restriction on the Company (our client), so the preferred position (no restriction at all) is not met. However, it sits squarely at the playbook fallback and should not be redlined. (1) Scope is limited to a named product set: the defined term \"Deerskin Products\" (which expressly excludes closeout merchandise and the Joan Cook Catalog per §1.1) plus named comparators Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled — this is not an undefined \"any competing business.\" (2) It is further confined to a single medium and format — \"any project similar to the Site on the Internet\" — leaving the Company's catalog, wholesale and bricks-and-mortar channels wholly unrestricted. (3) It runs \"during the term of this Agreement\" only, with no post-term tail, and the term under §4.1 is a one-year period auto-renewing annually and terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice, so the restraint is effectively capped at 12 months and we hold a unilateral exit. (4) Carve-outs exist: §6.2 preserves the Company's right to run its own closeout web site, the Deerskin Products definition excludes Joan Cook products, and §8(b) protects the existing Globix Agreement. Direction also favors us: the reciprocal covenant in §6.3 binds HDI on broader terms, with a two-year post-term tail that the Company does not bear, and the restriction is the consideration for HDI's exclusive-brand bargain. Nothing here approaches walk-away territory (no post-term non-compete and no undefined scope). Two minor sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: there is no express carve-out for internal development or for businesses acquired by the Company, and \"products substantially similar to Deerskin Products\" is somewhat elastic. If this agreement is reopened for other reasons, we would add an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out to §6.2, but neither point is material enough to justify a redline on its own.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-e8e225ca","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 6.1 binds the Company (our client) to exclusive dealing: it may not participate in any similar internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the \"Deerskin\" brand online. The restriction runs \"during the term of this Agreement,\" and Section 4.1 makes the term automatically renew for successive one-year periods indefinitely unless terminated on 90 days' notice, with Section 4.2 imposing a Termination Payment if the Company terminates. There is no service-level regime and no termination-for-breach right; the only performance-based exit (Section 1.6) is a one-off right if the Site is not operational within 70 days of signature, which lapses at launch. The result is exclusive dealing for the full (potentially perpetual) term with no ongoing performance-based exit — walk-away territory under this rule, and short of the fallback's 12-month cap and automatic release on failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. Because HDI grants a reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 (which benefits us and we leave intact), deleting the exclusivity outright would be disproportionate, so we redline to the fallback: a 12-month cap plus automatic termination of the restriction on any HDI delivery or performance failure. The product scope is tied to the defined term \"Deerskin Products\" and is acceptable; we note but do not separately flag the open-ended \"companies similar to\" wording.","proposal":"Confine Section 6.1 exclusivity to the defined Deerskin Products, cap it at 12 months, and release it automatically on HDI's service level or delivery date failure.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-govlaw-c175b77d","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 10.5 selects New York law with conflicts principles disclaimed, which is the playbook's preferred governing law. There is no arbitration provision anywhere in the agreement (no hits for \"arbitration\"), so disputes default to the courts rather than a foreign arbitral seat, and no foreign or vendor-home venue is imposed. The only shortfall against the preferred position is the absence of an express exclusive-venue designation for the state and federal courts in New York County; that is a missing sub-element rather than a material failure, since neither party is steered to an unacceptable forum. Noted for information only — we could add an exclusive New York County venue line if the document is reopened, but it does not warrant a redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-0440599a","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"The Agreement contains no intellectual property ownership provision. HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site (§1.1–1.3) and the Company supplies all Content (§2.1), but nothing states who owns the Site, the code and other work product developed for us, or the customer/user data generated through the Site. Section 5.2 gives us only artistic and editorial control, §6.1 is a limited trademark licence from us to HDI, and §8 treats Content and user information only as confidential — none of these confers ownership or a licence back. That leaves our deliverables and customer data unallocated, short of both the preferred and fallback positions.","proposal":"Insert a preferred-level ownership clause: Company owns and HDI assigns deliverables and work product, HDI retains pre-existing IP with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any HDI IP embedded in the deliverables, Company retains all rights in Company Data, no joint ownership.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-mfn-8fb93f10","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Searches for MFN-style language (\"most favored\", \"no less favorable\", \"favorable\", \"price\", \"discount\", \"third party\", \"terms\") return no provision requiring the Company to extend HDI pricing or terms no less favourable than those given to any third party, or to match third-party offers. The commercial terms are a fixed revenue share on Net Sales (Section 3.1), with no benchmarking or matching mechanic. The only related restriction is the Section 6.1 exclusivity covenant, which is a scope/exclusivity term rather than an MFN and is addressed under the exclusivity rule, not here. This meets the preferred position of no MFN obligation on the Customer, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-f1c0d846","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"The fee construct meets our preferred position: the Company owes HDI only a 30% revenue share on actual Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold, so all amounts are purely usage/sales-based. The $11,000 figure is a floor below which nothing is payable (a benefit to us), not a minimum spend or take-or-pay obligation, and there is no shortfall, minimum volume or minimum-order language anywhere in the Agreement. Term is one year with automatic one-year renewals terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice (§4.1), plus an immediate termination right if the Site is not live in 70 days (§1.6), so we are never locked into a multi-year commitment. Noted but not flagged here: the §4.2 Termination Payment (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000) is an exit cost payable only if we terminate, and the §6.1 exclusivity restricts competing Deerskin web projects — both are termination/exclusivity issues for their own rules rather than minimum purchase commitments, and neither creates a purchase obligation. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-b34368bd","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Searches for \"solicit\", \"hire\", \"induce\", \"recruit\", \"personnel\", \"staff\" and \"employ\" return no restrictive covenant on hiring anywhere in the Agreement; the only references to employees are in the confidentiality carve-out (p0051) and the independent-contractor clause (p0061), neither of which restricts the Company from soliciting or employing HDI personnel. The integration clause (p0069) confirms no other terms apply. This matches our preferred position of no non-solicitation or no-hire obligation binding the Company, so no redline is needed. The exclusivity covenant in Section 6.1 is a separate commercial restriction addressed under the exclusivity rule, not an employee non-solicit.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-04a745d4","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.1 provides automatic one-year (not multi-year) renewals, which is acceptable, and the Agreement contains no renewal price-uplift mechanic, so the pricing element of the rule is satisfied. However, the non-renewal notice window is ninety (90) days, which exceeds the fallback ceiling of 60 days (and the preferred 30 days), so the clause fails the fallback on a material term, though it stops short of walk-away territory. The redline moves the Company to a 30-day window while leaving HDI's 90-day period intact, so our exit flexibility improves without shortening the notice we receive; a 60-day Company window is an acceptable fallback. Note as a minor point only that there is no vendor renewal reminder mechanic.","proposal":"Cut the non-renewal notice window to 30 days and add a 60-day HDI renewal reminder with renewal increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-t4c-3dd5d199","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.1 gives each Party a convenience exit on ninety (90) days' written notice against a one-year auto-renewing term, which sits at the playbook fallback (Customer notice of 60-90 days; Vendor convenience only at end of term on 90 days' notice), so the notice mechanics themselves are acceptable and are not redlined. The material failure is the Termination Payment in Section 4.2(a): it applies only to Company terminations and is calculated as one half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — an uncapped exit penalty that can greatly exceed the 30% revenue-share fee we pay under Section 3.1, well beyond the fallback cap of three months' fees. It is also drafted to bite on any Company termination, including termination for HDI's default. We have capped the payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees and carved out terminations for HDI's breach and under Section 1.6.","proposal":"Cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees and confirm no payment on termination for HDI's default","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-warranty-9d5aebbe","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 9 is limited to mutual corporate-existence, authority, enforceability and no-conflict representations (p0056-p0057) plus an HDI acknowledgement regarding the Globix Agreement (p0058). Nothing in the Agreement contains an express HDI warranty that the design, development, hosting and maintenance services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, that the Site will conform to agreed specifications for any period, that HDI will comply with applicable law, or that the Site will be free of malicious code, and there is no repair/re-performance/refund remedy. Section 1.6 (operational deadline) and Section 5.2 (Company acceptance) are delivery and approval mechanics, not warranties. There is no disclaimer section, so this is not walk-away \"AS IS\" territory, but the absence of any express performance warranty falls short of even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies). Per the detection guidance, a missing express warranty is cured by insertion, so we propose a new Section 9(c) at the preferred position.","proposal":"Insert Section 9(c): HDI performance warranty with professional and workmanlike Services (90 days from performance), 12-month conformance of software and deliverables to documentation, compliance with laws and no malicious code, remedied by repair, replacement or refund.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-assign-02ea966e","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause. Two of the three playbook limbs are satisfied: nothing restricts the Company's assignment (so our affiliate/M&A flexibility is intact), and no provision anywhere (including the Section 4 termination provisions) gives HDI a termination or re-pricing right on our change of control — no change-of-control language appears in the document at all. However, the clause contains no consent standard at all, so HDI is free to assign this hosting and site-development arrangement to any third party, including a competitor of ours. The fallback requires consent for non-successor assignments not to be unreasonably withheld, so the clause fails the fallback on that material term. Minimal edit adds the preferred consent standard (with the affiliate/successor carve-out for us and an express statement that our change of control is not an assignment), leaving the existing sentence untouched.","proposal":"Insert preferred assignment consent standard after Section 10.3: Company free to assign to affiliates/successors, HDI needs our consent and cannot assign to a competitor, no HDI termination on our change of control.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-audit-8c7da5d6","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 3.4 is the only right of HDI to inspect Company records. It already satisfies several playbook elements: 30 days' prior written notice (better than the fallback's 15 days), inspection during normal business hours, a scope limited to payment-calculation records, HDI bearing its own inspection costs, and no right of access to Company systems. However, it contains no frequency limit, so HDI could inspect repeatedly at will; frequency (\"no more than once per 12 months\" / fallback \"once per year\") is a material term of both positions and unlimited audits are walk-away territory, so the clause fails the fallback. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development / Hosting Agreement with HDI)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review findings and recommended positions

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and recorded 18 findings: 5 compliant, 7 deviations and 6 rules for which no usable clause exists. The commercial architecture (30% revenue share on Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly floor, one-year auto-renewing term, mutual 90-day exit) is workable, and several rules are met outright — no MFN, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, no employee non-solicit, and New York law with no arbitration clause. The Section 6.1 field-of-use restriction on us also sits at the playbook fallback and we are not redlining it.

The risk is concentrated in what the Agreement omits and in the exit economics. There is no IP ownership provision (HDI builds and hosts the Site and holds our Content and user data, yet ownership of deliverables and Company data is unallocated), no performance warranty, no vendor indemnity, no insurance obligation, no limitation of liability and no transition-assistance or data-return mechanic. Separately, Section 4.2(a)'s Termination Payment (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) is an uncapped exit charge payable only by us and triggered by any Company termination, including termination for HDI's default; Section 6.1 exclusivity runs for a potentially perpetual term with no ongoing performance-based exit; Section 3.4 permits HDI records inspections with no frequency limit; and Section 10.3 lets HDI assign freely, including to a competitor.

Three redlines did not clear verification (Termination for Convenience, Audit, Limitation of Liability) and require manual drafting before the turn goes out.

Sits at the fallback; no redline. Absence of an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out noted only. | pass |

The failure is § 4.2(a): an uncapped exit payment payable only by us and biting even on termination for HDI's default. Cap at three months' § 3.1 fees and carve out termination for HDI's breach and under § 1.6. | **fail — redline requires manual drafting** |

Delete; if unavoidable, cap at three months' fees. | repaired |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No cap, no exclusion of indirect damages; both parties exposed to unlimited and consequential damages. Insert into § 9 (so it survives under § 10.7) a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, and uncapped Excluded Claims. | **fail — redline requires manual drafting** |
| Low | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | § 4 covers only notice and the Termination Payment; no exit, migration, data-return or deletion right, although HDI operates the Site on its own server and holds our data. Insert new § 4.3: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion. | repaired |

## Walk-away items

The following findings reach walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Exclusivity without a performance exit (§ 6.1 / § 4.1–4.2).** Exclusive dealing for the full, indefinitely renewing term with no service-level regime and no ongoing performance-based release. Must be capped at 12 months with automatic release on HDI delivery or performance failure.
2. **No HDI IP-infringement indemnity.** HDI designs, hosts and operates the Site and supplies the underlying software and technology; the total absence of any indemnity is unacceptable.
3. **No vendor insurance.** HDI processes user information and Company data under § 8.1; no coverage of any kind is a walk-away.
4. **Unlimited audit frequency (§ 3.4).** Inspections with no frequency cap are walk-away; the once-per-12-month limit is required.

We also treat the § 4.2(a) Termination Payment as a red-line-critical commercial item: as drafted it is uncapped, one-sided and payable even where we terminate for HDI's default.

## Next steps

1. **Manually draft the three unverified redlines** — T4C (§ 4.2(a) cap and breach carve-out), AUDIT (§ 3.4 frequency cap) and LOL-CAP (mutual cap into § 9) — before the turn is released; the automated edits did not verify.
2. **Confirm the insertions** for IP ownership, performance warranty (§ 9(c)), HDI indemnity (§ 9(c)), insurance (§ 10.9) and transition assistance (§ 4.3), and check that § 10.7 survival captures the new warranty, indemnity and liability provisions as intended.
3. **Brief the business** on the § 4.2 Termination Payment exposure at forecast Net Sales volumes so the negotiating team can price the exclusivity bargain against the exit cost.
4. **Confirm scope of use** for § 1.4 — identify which affiliates and contractors need access so the extended grant is drafted accurately.
5. **Hold as noted-only items** (raise only if the document is reopened): exclusive New York County venue, an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out to § 6.2, and a vendor renewal reminder mechanic.
6. **Send the turn** with the walk-away items flagged as gating, offering the stated fallbacks on exclusivity duration, renewal notice (60 days), indemnity (IP-only) and insurance limits."}
